noUnboundedLoops.note: Two loops in _skimSurplus (via _accrueSurplusShares and _distributeBuffer) iterate over the full strategy-owned `_authorizedClients` EnumerableSet with no pagination. Bound is owner-controlled: setClient(client, true) is the only growth path. Same bound as reflax-yield-vault-06 L-02; story-042 adds a SECOND parallel loop (`_distributeBuffer`) plus a fresh memory allocation `uint256[](clients.length)` on each skim, increasing per-iteration constant-factor cost but not the asymptotic bound.

checkedArithmetic.note: Solidity ^0.8.13; no unchecked blocks in this contract. New story-042 arithmetic: `shares * setAsideBufferSize[client] / 100` is bounded because `setAsideBufferSize <= 100` (enforced by `setSetAsideBuffer` in AYieldStrategy.sol#L255), and `shares` is already a uint256 in the range of vault share supply — no overflow risk in practice. `underlyingReceived * bufferShares[i] / totalShares` follows muldiv ordering (mul before div), preserving precision; rounding floors, dust accrues to `recipient` via `toRecipient = underlyingReceived - totalSetAside` (explicit comment confirms direction).

pauseMechanism.note: deposit/withdraw/skimSurplus carry whenNotPaused. depositAsOwner/withdrawAsOwner intentionally bypass pause (owner emergency action) — same behavior as baseline.

ceiInOrder.note: Pre-existing CEI deviations on _withdrawInternal and _totalWithdraw (state mutated AFTER external swap) — SLITHER-001/002 in baseline; covered by nonReentrant. UNCHANGED by story-042. NEW story-042 paths: _skimSurplus performs `safeIncreaseAllowance` and `ammAdapter.swap()` BEFORE the buffer-distribution transfers; principal accounting is never touched in any skim path (by design), so there is no state-mutation-after-call concern in the new code paths themselves. Each `safeTransfer` in _distributeBuffer goes to `clients[i]` (the protocol-owned client contract) — the loop body does not read or write contract storage, so even an ERC777-style hook in the underlying token (untrusted) cannot break the parallel array invariants.

snapshotSemantics.note: `totalValue` is snapshotted ONCE at line 421 (`vault.convertToAssets(vault.balanceOf(address(this)))`) and used for every per-client surplus computation in _accrueSurplusShares. `td = totalDeposited[token]` is also read once in both _skimSurplus and (re-read once) in _accrueSurplusShares. No re-snapshot inside the loop.

localFindings.description: story-042 introduces a parallel-array contract: `_accrueSurplusShares` populates `bufferShares[i]` for client `clients[i]`, then `_distributeBuffer` re-iterates the SAME `clients[]` array and indexes `bufferShares[i]` by position. Both calls are made within the same `_skimSurplus` invocation passing the SAME `clients` memory array (allocated by AYieldStrategy.skimSurplus from `_authorizedClients.values()`), so by construction `clients[i]` is identical between the two passes — no storage re-read of the EnumerableSet between passes, no reentrancy entry-point between passes (parent nonReentrant guard active). Verified local-safe; only flagged so downstream code-scanner can confirm no future refactor breaks the parallel invariant.
localFindings.recommendation: Consider an explicit struct{client, bufferShares}[] or `assert(clients.length == bufferShares.length)` defensive check in `_distributeBuffer` to lock in the contract. Not exploitable as written.

localFindings.description: `new uint256[](clients.length)` allocates fresh memory proportional to authorized-client count on every skim call. Composed with the now-double iteration (accrue + distribute), the per-skim gas cost is materially higher than the baseline (reflax-yield-vault-06) single-pass implementation. Same owner-controlled bound as L-02; documented for completeness — no new attack surface beyond what L-02 already covers.
localFindings.recommendation: None at protocol-owned client scale. If client set is expected to grow into the dozens, consider folding the buffer-share accumulator into the surplus-skim loop and replacing the parallel array with a per-client immediate transfer (BUT this changes the snapshot-then-swap-then-distribute ordering, which is currently correct for slippage attribution).

localFindings.description: Two floor-division points in the buffer payout: (a) `shares * setAsideBufferSize[client] / 100` in _accrueSurplusShares (line 487) — buffer percentages 1-99 round per-client buffer shares down; (b) `underlyingReceived * bufferShares[i] / totalShares` in _distributeBuffer (line 513) — proportional underlying allocation rounds down. Both round toward `recipient` (the skim caller / SYA) via `toRecipient = underlyingReceived - totalSetAside`. For very small surplus, sub-1-share buffer percentages, or tiny per-client buffer shares, individual `buf == 0` is explicitly skipped (line 514). Verified protocol-favoring direction; consistent with the existing rounding convention.
localFindings.recommendation: None. Behavior is documented in the function NatSpec ("dust (rounding) favors recipient").

localFindings.description: Local variable `shares` is reused: first holds surplus shares (line 485), then is reassigned to buffer shares (line 487) for the same iteration. The comment `// reuse slot: now buffer shares (0–100)` documents the intent, but a static-analysis reader (and downstream agents) may misread it as a bug. The `totalShares += shares` at line 486 happens BEFORE the reassignment, so the aggregate ceiling check at line 428 sees the correct (pre-buffer) surplus shares, not the buffer-reduced value. Verified correct.
localFindings.recommendation: Optional readability: rename to `bufShares` after reassignment, or inline the multiplication. Not a defect.

localFindings.description: `SurplusSkimmed(token, client, msg.sender, surplus, recipient)` is emitted with the SNAPSHOT surplus (vault-asset terms, pre-redeem), NOT the actual amount delivered. This was true in the baseline too. story-042 adds a wedge: when buffers are set, the recipient of part of the proceeds is `clients[i]` (the buffer holder), NOT the recipient parameter — but the event still names `recipient` as the receiver and reports the full snapshot surplus. External indexers that assume `SurplusSkimmed.amount` flowing to `SurplusSkimmed.recipient` will be wrong by `bufferShares[i] / totalShares * underlyingReceived` per surplus-bearing client. The CLAUDE.md note on the new return value documents the snapshot-vs-actual gap, but does NOT document the per-client buffer redirection in the event semantics. Flagged for code-scanner: this is a spec/behavior consistency note, not a local exploit.
localFindings.recommendation: Either (a) emit an additional `SurplusBufferedToClient(client, amount)` event in _distributeBuffer when buf > 0, or (b) extend `SurplusSkimmed` with a `bufferAmount` field. Defer the decision to code-scanner/severity-classifier — the underlying tokens are NOT lost (they reach the protocol-owned client), only the event topology shifts.

ceiInOrder.note: swap() ordering: pull tokenIn (line 132) -> approve router (line 135) -> exchange (line 138) -> emit (line 140). No storage state to protect; routes mapping is read-only in swap. The `Swapped` event after the external call (SLITHER-006) is event-ordering only — no exploitable surface.

localFindings.description: swap() uses `forceApprove(address(router), amountIn)` BEFORE calling router.exchange. If router.exchange reverts after the approve but before consuming all `amountIn` (or in an edge case where the router consumes less than amountIn), residual allowance to the trusted router remains. The forceApprove sets exactly amountIn each call, so the residual is overwritten on the next swap call — but in an idle period the adapter holds a non-zero allowance to a trusted external contract. Not exploitable as written (router is a trusted Curve contract, attacker cannot direct it to pull the leftover), and the every-call reset bounds the residual to the last call's amountIn. Flagged as defensive-coding low.
localFindings.recommendation: Optional: zero the router allowance at the end of swap (or use a try/catch around exchange that zeroes on revert). Not material at current trust level.

localFindings.description: tokenIn is pulled to the adapter (line 132) then forwarded to the router via exchange. tokenOut is sent BY THE ROUTER directly to msg.sender (line 138, receiver argument). If router.exchange reverts after pulling tokenIn from the adapter (via internal accounting), the adapter retains tokenIn. In normal Curve Router NG operation this does not happen — exchange is atomic — but it's worth surfacing to downstream agents that there is NO sweep function for stuck tokens on this adapter. Owner cannot recover dust.
localFindings.recommendation: Consider an owner-only `sweep(address token, address to, uint256 amount)` for stuck-token recovery, OR add a comment confirming the design choice that the adapter is intentionally non-custodial. Not exploitable.

localFindings.description: Path validation (lines 75-80) only checks `path[0] == tokenIn` and `lastNonZero == tokenOut`. It does NOT validate that the path is contiguously non-zero (i.e., that zeros only appear as padding at the tail), nor that pool addresses interleaved between tokens are non-zero. A malformed path with internal zeros could be set; correctness then relies entirely on the Curve Router NG rejecting it at exchange time. Because setRoute is onlyOwner and routes are deployment-time configuration verified off-chain against AMMRoutes.json, this is an integrity-check gap rather than an exploit surface.
localFindings.recommendation: Optional defense-in-depth: walk the path enforcing the interleaving invariant (token, pool, token, pool, ..., token, zero*) at set time. Current design accepts off-chain verification as the source of truth.

crossContractTrustBoundary.parentChild: ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy inherits AYieldStrategy. story-042 changes are SHARED across the parent (storage + setter + external skim signature) and the child (override implementation). Treat the new state variable `setAsideBufferSize` and external setter `setSetAsideBuffer` as parent-owned but child-read; the child's `_accrueSurplusShares` reads `setAsideBufferSize[client]` directly from parent storage (line 487). The child does NOT validate `setAsideBufferSize <= 100` — it relies on the parent's enforcement in `setSetAsideBuffer` (AYieldStrategy.sol#L255). If a future code path sets `setAsideBufferSize` bypassing the setter (none exists today), the `shares * setAsideBufferSize / 100` math could exceed `shares`. Verified safe under current code.
crossContractTrustBoundary.ammRoutesJsonConsumed: AMMRoutes.json is consumed by deployment scripts (not yet implemented per CLAUDE.md). Its correctness is a deployment-time concern; the on-chain contracts (CurveAMMAdapter.setRoute) accept any owner-signed payload, so the JSON only becomes binding when wired by a deployment script.
